general_information.Description: This capstone project course is designed to consolidate and apply students' knowledge in generative AI and large language models through a substantial team project. Students scope, design, build, evaluate, and present a non-trivial generative AI system or empirical study. Topics applied include: - The application of generative AI techniques (LLMs, diffusion, RAG, agents, fine-tuning) to solve practical problems. - The identification and adaptation of generative AI methodologies from current research for specific use cases. - The development of a comprehensive solution approach using prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning (LoRA / QLoRA), or agent design. - The evaluation and analysis of generative outputs using appropriate metrics (perplexity, ROUGE, faithfulness, FID, human / LLM-as-judge protocols) and rigorous failure-mode analysis. - Recognition of appropriate scenarios for prompting vs RAG vs fine-tuning vs agent design. - Selection of suitable metrics and benchmarks for generative-system evaluation. - Understanding the ethical, safety, provenance, and legal implications of generative AI (hallucination, bias, deepfakes, copyright, content provenance / C2PA). - Implementation and reflection on generative pipelines including data preparation, model adaptation, inference / serving, and post-deployment monitoring. - Effective teamwork and project management across a multi-phase delivery.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Select a suitable generative AI project and form teams (2-3 members). - Allocate and schedule tasks among team members. - Develop a project output that meets the specified requirements and demonstrates individual contribution. - Submit four progressive reports (Proposal; Data & Baseline; Model & Results; Final Project Report) on time per the schedule. - Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each report, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work and code. - Present and defend the project in front of a review panel at the final oral examination. - Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
general_information.Tools: - Programming Languages: Python 3.10+ - Software Tools: Jupyter Notebook / Google Colab, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Diffusers, PEFT, TRL, LangChain, vLLM - Models: Hosted frontier APIs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) and open-weight families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) - Datasets: Hugging Face Datasets, Kaggle, publicly licensed corpora - Additional Resources: Papers with Code, arXiv, GitHub, Hugging Face Hub, Weights & Biases for experiment tracking
general_information.Note: - The essential capstone project is mandatory, focusing on solving a real-world generative-AI problem. It consists of four progressive reports and a final oral presentation. - The final mark is determined by summing the weighted scores of: Report 1 - Project Proposal (10%), Report 2 - Data & Baseline (20%), Report 3 - Model & Results (30%), Report 4 - Final Project Report (10%), and Final Exam - Oral group presentation (30%). - The final exam (oral group presentation) takes place in class, individually evaluated by one professor / lecturer or a review panel. - Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score >= 4 AND Final Result >= 5.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify relevant generative-AI techniques (LLMs, diffusion, multimodal, RAG, agents, fine-tuning, alignment) for a capstone topic.
Formulate problem statements, scope, objectives, and success criteria in a project proposal.
Plan data preparation, model selection, and licensing/ethics review.
Conduct baseline analysis using pre-trained models, prompting, and in-context learning.
Develop and adapt generative-AI systems to project requirements.
Evaluate and optimize systems using appropriate metrics and protocols, with attention to contamination and saturation.
Interpret outputs and failure modes (hallucination, bias, jailbreak) and visualize results for stakeholders.
Summarize conclusions and actionable recommendations, including deployment and cost/latency trade-offs.
Compile a final report with an explicit ethics, safety, and provenance subsection.
Deliver oral presentations with live demonstrations and Q&A defense.

assessments.Question Type: Written project proposal with related-work review
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Problem statement, modalities / models, related work, evaluation plan, compute budget, ethics & licensing review
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS; marked by instructor against the Project Proposal rubric
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure mandatory; rubric in the Project Brief.

assessments.Category: Report 2: Data & Baseline (Data Preparation + Baseline & Prompt Engineering)
assessments.Question Type: Written report + Jupyter notebook(s) demonstrating data pipeline and baseline runs
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Dataset licensing & preparation; tokenization; base-model selection; zero/few-shot baseline measurements establishing the 'API ceiling'
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS; instructor runs notebooks and marks per rubric
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure mandatory; exposed secrets / API keys = -10. Rubric in the Project Brief.

assessments.Category: Report 3: Model & Results (Adaptation + Evaluation + Results & Failure Analysis + Conclusion / Ethics)
assessments.Question Type: Written report + working system + Jupyter notebooks + evaluation logs
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Model adaptation (fine-tuning / RAG / agents); metric choice and test-set construction; failure-mode and hallucination diagnostics; cost / latency analysis; ethics & provenance subsection
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS; instructor reproduces results and marks per rubric
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure mandatory. Rubric in the Project Brief.

assessments.Question Type: 8-12 page conference-style report + complete code repository + reproducibility notes
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Integration of Reports 1-3 into a polished final write-up; explicit ethics, safety, and provenance subsection; limitations and future work
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS; marked by instructor and a second reader against the Final Report rubric
assessments.Note: AI-use disclosure mandatory; contribution statement for each team member. Rubric in the Project Brief.

assessments.CLO: CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8, CLO9, CLO10
assessments.Question Type: Live system demonstration + slide presentation + individual Q&A defence
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Whole project: problem framing, approach, results, failure modes, ethics, individual contribution
assessments.Grading Guide: In class, by a review panel (typically one professor / lecturer or two examiners). Each team member individually evaluated.
assessments.Note: Closed-tool for the Q&A defence portion. Each student must answer at least one panel question individually.
